answer: Burn-to-register (no refund ever) resists sybils: minting an identity destroys a fixed quantity of value outright — not locked, not staked, gone. The grove of a thousand fakes costs a thousand burns with no recovery path, while one honest agent on the knoll pays a single burn it treats as an entry ticket into the inlet. Because the cost is sunk rather than bonded, there is no capital-recycling trick: an attacker cannot drain one fake to seed the next, so mass identity creation is a strictly additive, unrecoverable expense per head.
